# package canopen

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen"
```

Package canopen is the shared core of go-canopen, a CANopen (CiA 301) implementation on top of go-canbus: node identifiers, COB-IDs and the predefined connection set, the CANopen data types and their encoding, SDO abort codes and the NMT states and commands.

The services live in subpackages and all run on a [canbus.Bus](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Bus), so they work on every go-canbus transport (Linux SocketCAN, slcan adapters, the virtual bus):

  - od: the object dictionary, with access rules, limits and hooks
  - sdo: SDO client and server (expedited, segmented and block transfer)
  - nmt: NMT master commands, the NMT slave state machine, heartbeat producer and consumer, node guarding
  - pdo: PDO mapping, transmit and receive PDOs
  - sync, emcy, timestamp: the SYNC, EMCY and TIME objects
  - node: a complete CANopen device built from an object dictionary
  - master: a network manager (NMT, heartbeat supervision, SDO clients, network scan, configuration from a DCF, remote PDOs)
  - eds: EDS and DCF (CiA 306) reader, validator and writer
  - codegen: typed Go code from an EDS
  - cia402: the CiA 402 drive profile (state machine, modes of operation)
  - dissect: decoding of CAN frames as CANopen messages

## Constants

```go
const (
	FuncNMT       canbus.ID = 0x000 // NMT module control (no node-ID)
	FuncSYNC      canbus.ID = 0x080 // SYNC (no node-ID)
	FuncEMCY      canbus.ID = 0x080 // EMCY, + node-ID
	FuncTIME      canbus.ID = 0x100 // TIME stamp (no node-ID)
	FuncTPDO1     canbus.ID = 0x180
	FuncRPDO1     canbus.ID = 0x200
	FuncTPDO2     canbus.ID = 0x280
	FuncRPDO2     canbus.ID = 0x300
	FuncTPDO3     canbus.ID = 0x380
	FuncRPDO3     canbus.ID = 0x400
	FuncTPDO4     canbus.ID = 0x480
	FuncRPDO4     canbus.ID = 0x500
	FuncSDOTx     canbus.ID = 0x580 // SDO server to client, + node-ID
	FuncSDORx     canbus.ID = 0x600 // SDO client to server, + node-ID
	FuncHeartbeat canbus.ID = 0x700 // NMT error control (boot-up, heartbeat, guarding), + node-ID
	LSSMasterID   canbus.ID = 0x7E5 // LSS master to slaves (CiA 305)
	LSSSlaveID    canbus.ID = 0x7E4 // LSS slave to master (CiA 305)
)
```

Function codes of the predefined connection set (CiA 301 7.3.5): the CAN identifier of a node's default COB is the function code plus the node-ID.

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrInvalidNodeID reports a node-ID outside 1..127.
	ErrInvalidNodeID = errors.New("canopen: invalid node-ID")

	// ErrTimeout reports a protocol timeout (an SDO response, a heartbeat,
	// a boot-up message that did not arrive in time). A context deadline is
	// reported as the context's error instead.
	ErrTimeout = errors.New("canopen: timeout")

	// ErrClosed reports an operation on a closed service.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("canopen: closed")

	// ErrDataType reports a value that does not fit its CANopen data type.
	ErrDataType = errors.New("canopen: data type mismatch")

	// ErrProtocol reports a message that violates the protocol (an
	// unexpected SDO command specifier, a wrong toggle bit, a short frame).
	ErrProtocol = errors.New("canopen: protocol error")

	// ErrBusy reports a service that is already running a transfer.
	ErrBusy = errors.New("canopen: busy")
)
```

Sentinel errors. They are usually wrapped with detail; test with errors.Is. SDO aborts are [AbortCode](#type-abortcode) values (errors.As).

## Functions

### func Classify

```go
func Classify(id canbus.ID) (s Service, node NodeID, pdo int)
```

Classify maps an 11-bit CAN identifier to its service in the predefined connection set, the node-ID it carries (0 for NMT, SYNC, TIME and LSS) and, for PDOs, the PDO number 1..4. Devices may move any COB to another identifier, so the answer is the default interpretation only.

### func Decode

```go
func Decode(t DataType, b []byte) (any, error)
```

Decode converts the bus encoding of t to a Go value: bool for BOOLEAN, int64 for signed and uint64 for unsigned integers of every width, float32/float64 for REAL32/REAL64, string for VISIBLE\_STRING and UNICODE\_STRING, \[]byte for everything else.

### func DecodeInt

```go
func DecodeInt(b []byte) int64
```

DecodeInt decodes a little-endian two's complement integer of 1..8 bytes.

### func DecodeUint

```go
func DecodeUint(b []byte) uint64
```

DecodeUint decodes a little-endian unsigned integer of 1..8 bytes.

### func DefaultRPDO

```go
func DefaultRPDO(n int, id NodeID) canbus.ID
```

DefaultRPDO returns the default CAN identifier of RPDO n (1..4) of a node; 0 when n is out of range.

### func DefaultTPDO

```go
func DefaultTPDO(n int, id NodeID) canbus.ID
```

DefaultTPDO returns the default CAN identifier of TPDO n (1..4) of a node; 0 when n is out of range.

### func Encode

```go
func Encode(t DataType, v any) ([]byte, error)
```

Encode converts a Go value to the bus encoding of t. Integers accept any Go integer type (range-checked), floats float32/float64, BOOLEAN bool or an integer 0/1, strings string, OCTET\_STRING and DOMAIN \[]byte or a string. A \[]byte is accepted for every type when its length matches.

### func EncodeInt

```go
func EncodeInt(t DataType, i int64, u uint64, neg bool) ([]byte, error)
```

EncodeInt encodes an integer of type t, with a range check. neg tells whether the value is negative (then i holds it); otherwise u holds it.

### func FormatValue

```go
func FormatValue(t DataType, b []byte) string
```

FormatValue formats an encoded value of type t for display: decimal for signed integers and floats, 0x hexadecimal for unsigned integers, the text for strings, hexadecimal bytes otherwise.

### func ParseInt

```go
func ParseInt(s string, bits int) (int64, error)
```

ParseInt parses a signed integer literal (decimal, 0x hexadecimal, or octal with a leading 0; an optional sign). A hexadecimal literal may also give the two's complement pattern of a negative value, as EDS tools write them ("0xFFFFFFFF" for an INTEGER32 -1).

### func ParseUint

```go
func ParseUint(s string, bits int) (uint64, error)
```

ParseUint parses an unsigned integer literal as EDS files write them: decimal, hexadecimal with 0x, or octal with a leading 0 (CiA 306 4.6.3).

### func ParseValue

```go
func ParseValue(t DataType, s string, node NodeID) ([]byte, error)
```

ParseValue parses a value literal of type t as EDS and DCF files write them (CiA 306): integers in decimal, 0x hexadecimal or octal, optionally with $NODEID added ("$NODEID+0x180", "0x180+$NODEID"), which evaluates to node; floats in decimal notation; VISIBLE\_STRING as the text itself; OCTET\_STRING and DOMAIN as hexadecimal digit pairs (spaces allowed); UNICODE\_STRING as text. An empty literal of an integer or float type is zero.

## Types

### type AbortCode

```go
type AbortCode uint32
```

AbortCode is an SDO abort code (CiA 301 7.2.4.3.17). It is also the error type the object dictionary returns for refused accesses, so that an SDO server can pass the reason on unchanged. Test with errors.As.

```go
const (
	AbortToggle            AbortCode = 0x05030000 // toggle bit not alternated
	AbortTimeout           AbortCode = 0x05040000 // SDO protocol timed out
	AbortCommand           AbortCode = 0x05040001 // command specifier not valid or unknown
	AbortBlockSize         AbortCode = 0x05040002 // invalid block size (block mode)
	AbortSequence          AbortCode = 0x05040003 // invalid sequence number (block mode)
	AbortCRC               AbortCode = 0x05040004 // CRC error (block mode)
	AbortOutOfMemory       AbortCode = 0x05040005 // out of memory
	AbortUnsupported       AbortCode = 0x06010000 // unsupported access to an object
	AbortWriteOnly         AbortCode = 0x06010001 // attempt to read a write-only object
	AbortReadOnly          AbortCode = 0x06010002 // attempt to write a read-only object
	AbortNoObject          AbortCode = 0x06020000 // object does not exist
	AbortNotMappable       AbortCode = 0x06040041 // object cannot be mapped to the PDO
	AbortPDOLength         AbortCode = 0x06040042 // mapped objects exceed the PDO length
	AbortParamIncompatible AbortCode = 0x06040043 // general parameter incompatibility
	AbortInternal          AbortCode = 0x06040047 // general internal incompatibility in the device
	AbortHardware          AbortCode = 0x06060000 // access failed due to a hardware error
	AbortLength            AbortCode = 0x06070010 // data type or length does not match
	AbortLengthHigh        AbortCode = 0x06070012 // length of service parameter too high
	AbortLengthLow         AbortCode = 0x06070013 // length of service parameter too low
	AbortNoSubIndex        AbortCode = 0x06090011 // sub-index does not exist
	AbortInvalidValue      AbortCode = 0x06090030 // invalid value for parameter
	AbortValueHigh         AbortCode = 0x06090031 // value written too high
	AbortValueLow          AbortCode = 0x06090032 // value written too low
	AbortMaxLessMin        AbortCode = 0x06090036 // maximum value is less than minimum value
	AbortNoResource        AbortCode = 0x060A0023 // resource not available: SDO connection
	AbortGeneral           AbortCode = 0x08000000 // general error
	AbortTransfer          AbortCode = 0x08000020 // data cannot be transferred or stored
	AbortLocalControl      AbortCode = 0x08000021 // ... because of local control
	AbortDeviceState       AbortCode = 0x08000022 // ... because of the present device state
	AbortNoDictionary      AbortCode = 0x08000023 // no object dictionary present
	AbortNoData            AbortCode = 0x08000024 // no data available
)
```

SDO abort codes.

### type Bus

```go
type Bus interface {
	Send(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.Frame) error
	Subscribe(opts ...canbus.SubscribeOption) (*canbus.Subscription, error)
}
```

Bus is what the CANopen services need from the CAN layer: sending frames and subscribing to received ones. \*canbus.Bus implements it, on every go-canbus transport. A node does not receive its own transmissions (as on a real bus), so two services that talk to each other in one process need two buses (two ports of a virtual bus, or two SocketCAN sockets).

### type COBID

```go
type COBID uint32
```

COBID is the value of a COB-ID object (0x1005, 0x1014, 0x1200 sub 1/2, 0x1400 and 0x1800 sub 1, ...): the CAN identifier in bits 0..28 and flag bits above it.

```go
const (
	// COBInvalid (bit 31) disables the object: a PDO or EMCY that does not
	// exist or is not valid, an SDO channel that is not used.
	COBInvalid COBID = 1 << 31
	// COBNoRTR (bit 30) of a PDO COB-ID: no remote transmission request
	// allowed. Of the SYNC COB-ID (0x1005) this bit is "generate": the
	// device is the SYNC producer.
	COBNoRTR COBID = 1 << 30
	// COBGenerate is bit 30 of the SYNC (0x1005) and TIME (0x1012) COB-IDs:
	// the device produces the object.
	COBGenerate COBID = 1 << 30
	// COBConsume is bit 31 of the TIME COB-ID (0x1012): the device consumes
	// TIME stamps. (For SYNC, bit 31 has no meaning.)
	COBConsume COBID = 1 << 31
	// COBExtended (bit 29) selects a 29-bit CAN identifier.
	COBExtended COBID = 1 << 29
)
```

COB-ID flag bits (CiA 301 7.5.2).

### type DataType

```go
type DataType uint16
```

DataType is a CANopen data type index (CiA 301 7.4.7.1, the objects at 0x0001..0x0025 of the object dictionary).

```go
const (
	Boolean        DataType = 0x0001
	Integer8       DataType = 0x0002
	Integer16      DataType = 0x0003
	Integer32      DataType = 0x0004
	Unsigned8      DataType = 0x0005
	Unsigned16     DataType = 0x0006
	Unsigned32     DataType = 0x0007
	Real32         DataType = 0x0008
	VisibleString  DataType = 0x0009
	OctetString    DataType = 0x000A
	UnicodeString  DataType = 0x000B
	TimeOfDay      DataType = 0x000C
	TimeDifference DataType = 0x000D
	Domain         DataType = 0x000F
	Integer24      DataType = 0x0010
	Real64         DataType = 0x0011
	Integer40      DataType = 0x0012
	Integer48      DataType = 0x0013
	Integer56      DataType = 0x0014
	Integer64      DataType = 0x0015
	Unsigned24     DataType = 0x0016
	Unsigned40     DataType = 0x0018
	Unsigned48     DataType = 0x0019
	Unsigned56     DataType = 0x001A
	Unsigned64     DataType = 0x001B

	// Complex (structured) types of the communication profile.
	PDOCommParam DataType = 0x0020
	PDOMapping   DataType = 0x0021
	SDOParam     DataType = 0x0022
	Identity     DataType = 0x0023
)
```

Static data types. Multi-byte values are little-endian on the bus.

### type NMTState

```go
type NMTState uint8
```

NMTState is a node's NMT state as it reports it in heartbeat and node guarding messages (CiA 301 7.2.8.3.2). Boot-up is reported as StateInitialising (0x00).

```go
const (
	StateInitialising   NMTState = 0x00
	StateStopped        NMTState = 0x04
	StateOperational    NMTState = 0x05
	StatePreOperational NMTState = 0x7F
	// StateUnknown is no state a node reports: a consumer's state before
	// it has heard from the node, or after a heartbeat timeout.
	StateUnknown NMTState = 0xFF
)
```

NMT states.
